tb21_profile.skill: Implement a distributed training algorithm from a prose spec: split a transformer's layers into balanced stages, hand-roll P2P forward/backward tensor exchange, drive autograd across a stage boundary with an incoming grad, and scale the loss by the microbatch count so accumulated grads match the full batch
tb21_profile.domain: PyTorch: torch.distributed (P2POp/isend/irecv, rank, world_size), HuggingFace LlamaForCausalLM internals, autograd, dtype/device placement
tb21_profile.task_form: implement-from-spec of a published algorithm (AFAB pipeline schedule) with a numerical-equivalence test against a reference model; multi-step, no starter code

verifier_notes: No grade overturned. Worth flagging for the merge: the closest-by-topic CalibForge candidate software-engineering_20260509_205636_024 (implement a torch.autograd.Function with a correct custom backward - the single most transferable sub-skill for driving backward across a pipeline stage) is graded FREE, so it is excluded from final_top10 and from per_source. Terminal-Lego's three most on-topic PyTorch tasks (task_13140 gradient clipping, task_13149 Adam vs AdamW, task_05502 CUDA memory leak in an inference loop) are also FREE despite 10-18 tests each. software-engineering_20260604_003113_023 (MoE layer from spec) is graded weak at 0.214 over 14 tests; the instruction is 4.1k chars of precise numeric spec, so the grade probably understates it, but I left it out of final_top10 anyway rather than argue.

Use mpi4py to split MCMC chains over ranks and combine the per-rank results; rank/world_size reasoning plus a correctness check on the merged output.
Write an MPI script run as mpiexec -n N that divides a file set across ranks and reduces results; same launch-with-N-ranks test harness shape.
Build a parallelised sampler over at least four workers whose combined estimate must match the reference parameters; parallel decomposition with numeric verification.
Reconstruct an undocumented PyTorch nn.Module from a checkpoint's key/shape layout and run it; requires reading a model's layer structure, which stage-splitting also needs.
Rebuild a torch model from saved weights so the regenerated embeddings match a reference exactly; numeric-equivalence-against-reference testing like this TB2.1 task.
Load weights into a torch network and run inference over many inputs; torch module and tensor handling, no distribution or backward.
Infer a torch.nn.Sequential architecture from checkpoint keys and shapes; layer-structure reasoning only, forward pass only.
Fix a buggy PyTorch model definition so the supplied weights load and predictions match; shape-mismatch debugging in torch.
MPI-parallel numerical integration validated against the analytic value; rank-partitioned compute with a pinned numeric answer, no autograd.

Operations mis-tracked in the computation graph during flop counting; forces reasoning about what torch actually executes per op.

Module hierarchy printed in reverse order; fix requires understanding torch's nested module traversal order.
Tensor shape handling broken in to_numpy; dimension bookkeeping across tensor conversions.
Running mean and variance not updated correctly; stateful-layer semantics that also decide whether a split model trains identically.
smooth_l1_loss degenerates for tiny beta; numerically careful loss implementation, adjacent to the scaled cross-entropy here.
giou_loss fails on empty tensors; edge-case handling in a torch loss, weak transfer beyond the domain.
PeriodicCheckpointer misbehaves; training-loop plumbing in a PyTorch utility library.
Dask graph/partitioning behaviour; chunked parallel computation over a task graph, different framework and no gradients.

CalibForge.reason: Multi-task DDP training with gradient checkpointing under torchrun --nproc_per_node=2 fails; same 2-rank harness, same forward/backward-across-processes debugging.
DDP weights silently diverge between ranks; requires reasoning about when gradients actually synchronise, the crux of any hand-rolled parallel scheme.
Make gradient accumulation exactly equal large-batch training; that is the loss-scaled-by-number-of-microbatches requirement in this TB2.1 spec.
batch_size=8 versus 2x4 accumulation must produce identical gradients; pins the microbatch loss-normalisation rule with strong tests.
Write forward and backward by hand with no autograd; the manual chain-rule reasoning needed to hand off grads between pipeline stages.
DDP plus gradient checkpointing crashes with 2 spawned processes on a multi-forward model; reentrant-backward debugging in a real 2-rank setup.
Accumulated versus full-batch training on variable-length sequences must match; token-count-aware loss normalisation, strongly tested.
A hand-written backward for a custom activation is subtly wrong and only shows up as slow convergence; exactly the silent-gradient-bug class here.
Implement an MoE layer with router and load balancing into /app/moe.py from a long numeric spec; same write-a-transformer-component-from-spec genre.
Embedding shape mismatch under 8-way tensor parallelism; the only sharding-a-model-across-ranks debugging task in the whole pool.

Model parameters diverge across ranks with no error raised; trains the habit of checking cross-rank agreement, which pipeline stages need.
Implement forward and backward passes by hand without autograd; the chain-rule reasoning for passing grads back over a stage boundary.
Prove and fix gradient equivalence between one big batch and accumulated microbatches; strong pinned tests on the exact normalisation rule.
DDP with gradient checkpointing crashes when one model runs several forwards per step; multi-forward-then-backward scheduling, as AFAB does.
A wrong hand-written backward shows up only as slow convergence; teaches verifying a manual gradient against a reference, which this test does.
Debug embedding shape mismatches under 8-way tensor parallelism; the only model-sharded-across-ranks task anywhere in the pool.
Partition a large structure into roughly balanced sub-domains for parallel workers; the balanced-layer-split decision that opens this TB2.1 task.
Distribute work across mpi4py ranks and recombine per-rank results into one verified answer; rank/world_size decomposition with a numeric check.

notes: This is the clearest case yet for the two new corpora. A regex for torch.distributed|P2POp|all_reduce|DistributedDataParallel|pipeline parallel|tensor parallel over all 56,307 v1 instructions returns exactly ONE hit (tqdm__tqdm-617, a tqdm/DataLoader display conflict). The same regex over the new corpora returns four real distributed-PyTorch training tasks in CalibForge plus one in Terminal-Lego. CalibForge also owns a large, well-verified gradient-accumulation-equivalence cluster (at least 15 tasks) that is the best available proxy for the microbatch loss-scaling requirement, and a hand-written-backward cluster that is the best proxy for driving autograd across a stage boundary. Eight of my final ten are CalibForge and I would happily have made it nine. Nothing anywhere in the 76,786-task pool implements pipeline parallelism, P2P send/recv, or an AFAB/1F1B schedule, so the true crux of this TB2.1 task is uncovered; the best we can offer is DDP correctness plus manual backward plus balanced partitioning as three separate half-matches. TerminalWorld is the corpus where I could not find ten defensible candidates: it has no PyTorch training content at all, so entries 4-10 there are honest filler scored 1-2 and should be ignored at merge time rather than treated as a ranked list. Recursive-Task-Synthesis is nearly as bad - one PyTorch task (rts_task_956ea2e372fe004edbe0d44d) and a handful of mpirun-a-C-program chores; its retrieval shortlist was dominated by a pyperaptor 'parallel pipeline' cluster that is a pure lexical false positive on the words pipeline and parallel, and I dropped all but two of those. SWE-Smith's fvcore cluster is a legitimate PyTorch-domain match (module-tree traversal, flop/parameter accounting) but is fix-a-bug shaped, so it caps out at overall 3. TerminalWorld filler note: I swapped out tw_12007 for tw_479699 purely to keep a FREE grade out of the list; neither is a real match.
